chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Abu Jamilyah from Zayd al-Shahham, Abu Usamah, who said:

I asked him about a man who prayed Asr for six rak'at or five rak'at. He said: 'If he is certain that he prayed five or six, let him repeat [the prayer]. And if he does not know whether he added or decreased, let him say Takbir while sitting, then bow for two rak'at, reading in them the Opening of the Book, at the end of his prayer, then he sits for Tashahhud. And if he is certain that he prayed two or three, then departed and spoke, and did not know that he had not completed the prayer, it is upon him to complete what remained of it. For the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed with the people two rak'at, then forgot until he departed. So Dhul-Shimalayn said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, did something new happen in the prayer?' He said: 'O people, did Dhul-Shimalayn speak the truth?' They said: 'Yes, you did not pray except two rak'at.' So he stood and completed what remained of his prayer.'

key_terms.ذُو الشِّمَالَيْنِ: Dhul-Shimalayn (a companion known for having two left hands or limbs)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they are unsure whether they prayed five or six rak'at during Asr?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the jurisprudence of *sahw* (forgetfulness) in the Asr prayer, distinguishing between certainty of error, which mandates full repetition, and doubt, which requires completing the missing rak'at. It grounds these rulings in the Prophetic precedent of the *Sahw al-Nabi*, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) completed his prayer after being reminded by Dhul-Shimaytain, establishing the principle of validating the prayer through subsequent completion rather than immediate repetition.
